# Alpha documentation

> Technical documentation for **Alpha**, the open-source autonomous multi-agent AI
> operating system. A LangGraph agent runtime behind a FastAPI Gateway, with a
> Next.js 15 workspace and an Electron Windows desktop app. 139 native tools, 49
> middleware modules, MCP
> extensions, 24 public skills, sandboxed execution, persistent memory, and nine
> messaging channels. Self-hosted, MIT licensed.

Canonical repository: https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha
Maintainer: Prem Kumar (https://github.com/itsPremkumar) · License: MIT · Version: 2.1.0

This file is the docs-scoped `llms.txt` index. For the repository overview see
the [root `/llms.txt`](../llms.txt); for expanded context see
[`/llms-full.txt`](../llms-full.txt).

## Start here

- [Getting started](GETTING_STARTED.md): prerequisites, install methods for every platform, first run, and verification.
- [Production readiness transfer guide](https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/docs/PRODUCTION_READINESS_TRANSFER_GUIDE.md): current handoff evidence, startup incident, honest goal/evidence boundaries, and a copy-ready continuation prompt.
- [Agent response workspace](https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/README.md#8-presentation-layer-desktop--web-ui): inspectable tool and subagent progress cards, readable latest subagent step/tool-call summaries, transcript search/export, run-product side pane, and autonomous command receipts with Gateway execution status and returned output; detection alone is not proof of execution.
- [FAQ](FAQ.md): short, citable answers to the most common questions.
- [Comparison](COMPARISON.md): Alpha vs LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, OpenHands, and Dify, plus a selection decision guide.
- [Use cases](USE_CASES.md): concrete end-to-end jobs mapped to the subsystem that delivers each.
- [Glossary](GLOSSARY.md): every Alpha term defined in one page, with caveats marked.
- [Discoverability](DISCOVERABILITY.md): how this project is optimized for SEO, GEO, and AEO.

## Architecture

- [Architecture](https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): runtime planes, the middleware chain, sandbox tiers, and the 127 harness engine packages.
- [Arena tournaments](https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/docs/ARENA.md): one task, N strategy-carded sub-agents, a durable single-elimination bracket with the call arithmetic, confirmation gate, judge blinding, hard gates, and the honest limits of what a tournament proves.
- [Capability mesh](https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/docs/CAPABILITY_MESH.md): the 23 library modules by phase, the 12 model-tool actions (one write), the `/api/capability-mesh` routes, the `enabled: false` config slice, and the honesty boundaries — a read/preview plane where nothing is dispatched.
- [Group-relative orchestration](ALPHA_GRPO_INSPIRED_ORCHESTRATION_PLAN.md): a bounded group of candidate attempts under distinct strategies, absolute-gate eligibility (relative rank only ranks the eligible), one bounded repair round, and an explicit UNVERIFIED partial result when nothing passes; `swarm` tool `compete`/`compete_status`, off by default behind `gro.enabled`.
- [Dynamic workflows](DYNAMIC_WORKFLOWS.md): the typed, evidence-gated workflow runtime and its honest execution labels.
- [APEX Autopilot](https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/docs/APEX_AUTOPILOT.md): goal sessions, Gateway RunManager dispatch, run/token observation, UI/API submission of complete owner-evaluated acceptance evidence, registered probes, and automatic exact-text/artifact readbacks plus the typed auto-detected project-test criterion from a complete correlated run-event scan; supplied test commands and arbitrary criteria remain unverified until a supported collector or owner evidence covers them. The UI narrows new sessions to editable 100,000-token, 200-tool-call, and 60-minute ceilings; expanded session history shows those ceilings beside usage, and one in-flight model call may cross the token ceiling. API clients that omit a budget inherit unlimited profile limits. Also: bounded admin replans, APEX task-delegation caps, and separate durable `batch_task` limits.
The APEX invariant endpoint checks module/symbol presence and does not prove that runtime paths invoke the guards.
APEX session, mode, and goal snapshots use same-host local file locking; goal decomposition saves the child and parent link atomically in one snapshot. This is not cross-host exactly-once execution. Automatic APEX evidence recognizes only exact-quoted-text readback, declared non-empty artifact readback, and the typed auto-detected project-test criterion from a complete correlated run scan; it does not verify arbitrary natural-language criteria. Test evidence requires a successful argv receipt, no caller-supplied command, exit code zero, and zero failures. Other command and HTTP evidence collectors remain explicitly selected by a caller.
- [Conversation goal completion](https://github.com/itsPremKumar/alpha/blob/main/backend/packages/harness/alpha/runtime/goal.py): the bounded conversational goal loop evaluates visible chat together with persisted successful tool receipts, treats tool output as untrusted data, and remains distinct from measured APEX acceptance verification.
- [Alpha Mod Kernel](https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/docs/ALPHA_MOD_KERNEL_MASTER_SPECIFICATION.md): ordered lead-agent lifecycle middleware, explicit capability grants, fail-closed emergency stop and risk gates; held actions are durable single-process JSON with an admin approve/reject route, while the kernel journal, storage, and timers remain process-local.
Operator console: the Mods workspace view renders the ordered chain and each mod's describe, runs contributed mod commands, and (admin-gated) the audit ledger plus hold queue; POST /api/mods/preview bounds what a tool call would touch and never executes it, and an absent list is reported as absent rather than as empty.
- [Extensions](EXTENSIONS.md): MCP over stdio/HTTP/SSE plus the Python extension contribution contract.
- [MCP Server](https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/backend/docs/MCP_SERVER.md): setup, policy, routing hints, and deferred schema discovery for MCP and first-party tools.
- [Skills](SKILLS.md): skill packages, the curator lifecycle, quarantine trust tiers, and the 24 public skills.
- [Voice conversation](VOICE_CONVERSATION.md): the real-time local voice loop (Whisper + Piper, no paid speech API).
- [Workforce](WORKFORCE.md): bot roster, SOUL protocol, DMs, swarm DAG runtime, projects with owner-scoped per-run project instructions, Kanban, Bot Forge, and UI guidance for choosing subagent limits, swarm topologies, Arena competitor counts, and when each fits.
- Swarm task results display the Gateway's acceptance status in Team Ops; task completion without declared acceptance criteria is explicitly unverified.
- Specialist swarm reports include an advisory receipt-citation audit; action claims without citations or with unresolved citations are surfaced as uncorroborated, and call receipts are not treated as proof of claim correctness.
- Swarm creation reports the decomposer's predicted critical path and speedup; a plan estimated to exceed its declared wall-clock budget is refused before registration. Token and tool-call projections remain unmeasured.
- Team Ops distinguishes requested model overrides from model labels recorded in worker evidence; the UI does not infer a model that the Gateway did not report.
- Team Ops' swarm structure panel reports measured task overlap and meaningful completion from Gateway telemetry; unknown values and metric-read failures remain distinct, and the advisory signals do not verify correctness. Nonterminal swarm rows refresh every three seconds without reloading unrelated panels.
- The swarm API and Team Ops support up to 1,000 explicit work items and a requested concurrency ceiling of 1,000. Actual overlap depends on ready-task count, local executor/provider capacity, and run budgets; see the [Workforce guide](https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/docs/WORKFORCE.md#choosing-a-method-and-its-size-in-the-ui).
- [Per-bot model configuration](BOT_MODEL_CONFIG.md): each bot's primary model, fallback chain, counselling and mixture panels, named only from `config.yaml` `models[]`.
- [Lion companion](LION_COMPANION.md): the local-first Milo companion and its presentation contract.
- [Run recovery](RUN_RECOVERY.md): durable checkpoints, lease fencing, and safe replay.
- [Durable runtime](architecture/durable-runtime.md): connectivity as a first-class state, sessions parked rather than failed, and unbounded network waits (`network_wait.max_attempts: 0`).
- [Peer network](ALPHA_PEER_NETWORK.md): Alpha-to-Alpha discovery, explicit pairing, locally rendered/scanned QR invites, and direct delivery; disabled by default.

## Reasoning and memory

- [Cognitive engines](COGNITIVE_ENGINES.md): AVO, Mixture of Agents, Theory of Mind, epistemic belief tracking, and dreaming.
- [Deep research](DEEP_RESEARCH.md): the five-pass search pipeline, gap filling, and the citation contract.
- [System One](SYSTEM_ONE.md): the fast structured decision layer (typed choice/score/noul).
- [System One calibration](SYSTEM_ONE_CALIBRATION.md): calibration methodology and trust measurement.
- [System One use cases](SYSTEM_ONE_AGENT_USE_CASES.md): agentic use-case research for System One models.
- [System One roadmap](SYSTEM_ONE_ALPHA_ROADMAP.md): implementation roadmap for System One.
- [System One laptop control](SYSTEM_ONE_LAPTOP_CONTROL_IDEAS.md): computer-use architecture and Alpha's fit.
- [System One browser eval](SYSTEM_ONE_BROWSER_AGENT_EVAL.md): measured evaluation of a browser agent.
- [Memory](https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/docs/MEMORY.md): layered memory, task-aware typed recall (opt-in), trusted-workspace code structure memory (default-off), L1 credential redaction limits, prospective reminders, and fail-closed memory-fabric deletion.
- [Hy-Memory 2.0 adoption plan](ALPHA_HY_MEMORY_2_ADOPTION_PLAN.md): feature-by-feature comparison against Tencent's dual-process memory system, phased default-off adoption plan, and what Alpha must not adopt.
- [Memory types](MEMORY_TYPES.md): the canonical memory taxonomy and Alpha's coverage of it.
- [Memory fabric plan](MEMORY_FABRIC_PLAN.md): memory fabric boundaries and deferred work.
- [Third-party memory notices](THIRD_PARTY_MEMORY_NOTICES.md): subsystem-level attribution for adapted memory code.
- [Reasoning plan](REASONING_PLAN.md): the default-off reasoning plane, its contracts, and its budgeting.
